title: test: route source-scanning tests through the shared comment mask (#9183)
body:
Converts the source-scanning tests that hand-roll a private comment stripper to the shared
`scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`. **Tests only — no runtime code changes.**

`Refs #9183` rather than `Fixes`: 29 of the 32 carriers are converted, and the remaining
three are a deliberate exclusion explained under "What is left, and why" below.

## Step 1 — the population was re-derived, not inherited

Neither figure in the card survived measurement: the card said **6**, triage said "at least 8,
maybe 12". The real count is **32**.

The discriminant triage asked for is *"does this code read a source file and decide something
from what it read?"* — never the spelling of a regex. It was applied in three mechanical halves:

1. **Is it a comment stripper?** Every regex used as a `.replace()` pattern is *executed*
   against marker probes and counts only if it removes a marker sitting inside a comment while
   leaving the surrounding code intact. This is behavioural, so glob regexes, character
   classes and route regexes drop out on their own — `plugin-grid/src/importParsers.ts`'s
   `/[()（）[\]{}:：,，、/*＊]/g` is excluded because the marker survives it.
2. **Is the hit real code?** The census masks each file with `js-comment-mask.mjs` itself
   before looking, so a stripper named *in prose* is structurally invisible.
3. **Does it read source?** Checked, then each survivor was classified by hand.

**Controls, in the same command.** Positive: all six carriers named on the card and both
carriers triage found (`guide-layout-app-shell-doc.test.ts:194`,
`readme-calendar-view-schema.test.ts:96`) are present. Negative: triage's prose non-carrier
`readme-flow-canvas-draft.test.ts:108` is absent — and it does still contain the shape, in a
docblock, so the exclusion is real rather than accidental. Excluding string/template bytes as
well changed nothing, so no hit was a test fixture.

### Two premises measured FALSE

- **The card's shape column is wrong for two of its own six.** `expandableFamily.identity-5692`
  (L208-209) and `spec-ui-schema-reexports` (L195-196) are listed "line only" but are block+line
  naive pairs. Five of the card's six are block+line, not three.
- **Triage's shape reading is wrong for one.** `readme-calendar-view-schema` is called line-only
  but is block+line (L95-96).

So the block+line group — the one spelling verbatim the expression the module header quotes as
its failing example — is **22 files**, not the "at least 4" the dispatch expected.

## Step 2 — the verdict diff, which gated everything after it

Each carrier's own stripper was extracted from its source, **executed**, and compared against
`maskComments` on **exactly the files that carrier reads** (scan sets derived per carrier; the
tree-wide comparison was discarded as too coarse to mean anything).

**Result: no carrier gives a wrong answer today. The card stays p3.**

| carrier group | verdict |
|---|---|
| 23 carriers | stripper output identical to `maskComments` on every file scanned |
| 5 carriers | stripper **does erase real code** on a file it scans — but no erased span carries the signal the test decides from |

The five that do lose code, and what they lose:

- `feedTypeProducerCensus-5877` → `RecordDetailView.tsx` loses exactly two lines, both regex
  literals (`/^https?:\/\//i`, `/\/api\/v1\/auth\//`). The census looks for `type: '<kind>'`
  producers; neither line holds one.
- `actions-envelope.ratchet` and `flow-envelope.ratchet` → re-derived **both ways**: identical
  offender lists (`[]`) and identical caller sets
  (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, `FlowRunner.tsx`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`).
- `flow-node-producers.label` → 3 of the 127 files it scans, all inside placeholder strings such
  as `placeholder={'// (input, ctx) => result\nreturn { ok: true }'}`. The `label` token count is
  identical either way (107/107, 18/18, 105/105).
- `expandableFamily.identity-5692` → `ObjectDataTable.tsx`, an SVG URL. All five of its
  assertions read identically before and after.

That is a sharper statement than the card's honest "no input in the tree makes any of them give
a wrong answer": several of them **are** already reading less than they think. It just is not yet
code that matters — which is exactly the state that ends the moment someone edits one of those
files.

## Step 3 — the import cost, measured before scoping

The card's one explicitly unmeasured item. Both packages resolve and type-check the
`../../../../scripts/*.mjs` import exactly as `app-shell` and `plugin-kanban` already do:

| package | `pnpm --filter … run type-check` |
|---|---|
| `@object-ui/types` | exit 0 |
| `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` | exit 0 |

⚠️ The first `plugin-dashboard` run failed with `TS2307: Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'`
— **stale `dist`, not the import**. After building its dependency closure it is clean. Worth
recording because that failure reads exactly like a broken cross-tree import and is not one.

All three test configs extend the root `tsconfig.json`, which leaves `allowJs` unset, so the
`@ts-expect-error` on the import is *consumed* rather than reported unused — the same reason
the precedent needs it.

## Step 4 — the conversion

29 files. Each keeps its local helper name and call sites; only the body changes, plus the
import block the two precedents already established:

```ts
// @ts-expect-error — plain-JS shared helper, intentionally untyped (`allowJs: false`)
import { maskComments } from '<…>/scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs';

/** Local annotation, since the import above is untyped — the call site stays checked. */
const mask: (source: string) => string = maskComments;
```

**Line-only carriers converted too** (`filter-builder-mirror-6939`, and the line-only halves of
the pairs). Judgement, and the reason is `filter-builder-mirror-6939` itself: it carries four
lines of prose reasoning about the index shift its stripper causes — *"stripping SHORTENS the
block, so an index taken before the strip addresses a different place after it"*. `maskComments`
blanks rather than deletes, so every byte offset and line number survives. That hazard is now
**structurally impossible** for a converted reader rather than carefully avoided, which is the
structural improvement the card flagged and it applies to line-only carriers just as much.

## What is left, and why

Three carriers are deliberately **not** converted, because their stripper is not pointed at
JavaScript:

| carrier | target |
|---|---|
| `empty-base-classes-override-friendly-8525` | CSS (`packages/components/src/index.css`) |
| `ci-cd-pipeline-doc` | Markdown + `.github/workflows/*.yml` |
| `skill-guide-data-table-binding` | JSONC, fed to `JSON.parse` |

`js-comment-mask.mjs` answers "is this span a comment, or code?" **for JavaScript** — its scanner
knows JS strings, templates and regex literals. Pointing it at CSS or YAML would substitute a new
guess for the shared answer, in the same spirit as the defect this card is about. Naming them
here rather than silently converting them.

## Tests

- **29 converted suites: 29 files passed, 312 tests passed.** No test was skipped, disabled or
  weakened; no assertion was edited.
- Type-check: 12 affected packages, all exit 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint .` — **4907 files, 0 errors** (12865 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings,
  unchanged; warnings do not fail the gate).
- Gates: `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:control-bytes`,
  `check:test-path-roots`, `check:doc-example-readers` — all exit 0.
- `check:comment-mask-corpus` was **not** widened to watch these files. Its subject is the
  masker's own correctness, not who uses it; a "who isn't using the masker" guard is a different
  card and by repair order comes after this conversion.

### One gate is red for a reason that is not this diff

`check:node-esm-load` exits 1, refusing 2 of 37 entries on **provenance**: turbo replayed
`@object-ui/auth` and `@object-ui/react-runtime` from another worktree's shared cache
(`/home/user/objectui-issue-7848`). The gate says so itself and names `--force-build` as the
remedy. Its subject is published ESM entries; every file in this diff is a `*.test.ts(x)`, so the
subjects are disjoint.
